title: WISE GRANOLA GOODS
subtitle: Building the online storefront for my own granola business in San Diego — one-time orders and box subscriptions, all running on Square and shaped around a real weekly bake schedule.

sections.title: The problem
body: WISE GRANOLA GOODS sells at San Diego farmers markets and through local delivery. I wanted customers to be able to order ahead or subscribe online, with prices that still work for the business.
So the site isn't just a storefront: the product rules, pricing, and order cutoffs all come from how the business actually runs each week.

sections.title: The weekly cycle the site is built around
sections.caption: Ordering closes before ingredients are bought, so every batch is baked to real demand.

events: La Mesa Village Farmers Market, 3–7 PM

rows: La Mesa Village Farmers Market (La Mesa Blvd, 4th St–Palm Ave)

sections.title: Margin targets by channel
sections.caption: Subscriptions trade a few points of margin for predictable weekly volume.

sections.title: Business rules I encoded
items: Fixed-price box subscriptions through Square Subscriptions, covering both pickup and delivery.
Two cadences only — every 2 weeks or monthly — to keep baking predictable.
Volume discounts with a minimum order, priced so retail increases stay within $1–2.
No commercial-kitchen rent in the cost model, which is what keeps the 40% target realistic.
Orders not picked up within 2 weeks are discarded and still charged.
Glass jars and refills stay in-person only at the market.

sections.title: Why it's in a data portfolio
sections.body: Every price on the site comes out of a cost-and-margin model, and the order cutoff exists so purchasing matches demand. It's the same thinking as an analytics project — just with my own money on the line.
